did_you_know.text: The word “Aviv” refers to the stage when barley grains ripen, reflecting the ancient connection between the calendar and agriculture. In later periods, this month was also called Nisan.
The phrase “bread of affliction” presents matzah as simple, humble bread—not merely bread that did not have time to rise. It became a symbol of remembering hardship and the journey to freedom.
The word “kammah” means grain standing in the field, while a “chermesh” is a harvesting sickle. Counting seven weeks connects the beginning of the barley harvest with Shavuot.

The Levite is included because the tribe of Levi did not receive a regular territorial inheritance like the other tribes. Festivals therefore provided an opportunity to strengthen communal responsibility toward those without farmland.

In the Bible, “judges” are responsible for deciding cases, while “officers” are associated with carrying out and supervising the authorities’ decisions. This shows an early distinction between making a decision and enforcing it.

The repetition “justice, justice” emphasizes that justice is not a one-time goal but a path to pursue continually. The Sages also understood it as a reminder that even the means used to achieve justice must be just.

An “Asherah” was a Canaanite cult symbol, sometimes represented as a sacred tree or pole associated with fertility worship. The prohibition sets worship of God apart from religious practices common in the surrounding region.
